record.paper_title: Ten Open Problems in Connexive Logic
record.original_question: Carry out a systematic investigation, in the style of Spinks and Veroff, of systems related to the connexive logic C, focusing on the contraposable conditional, and determine which of those systems are especially interesting because they connect C-like systems with relevance logics.

evidence.quote: Open problem 6 Can we carry out the systematic investigations for systems related to C by following Spinks and Veroff? Are there particularly interesting systems related to C that are related to relevance logics by focusing on the contraposable conditional? If so, which ones?
there is at least one reason to be interested in the contraposable conditional in C and related systems

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Connexive logic C is a propositional logic obtained from a positive intuitionistic-like base equipped with a strong (involutive) negation ~ and a conditional →, in which the standard clauses for negated conditionals are modified so that the connexive theses

  (Aristotle)  ~( ~A → A )  and  ~( A → ~A ),
  (Boethius)   (A → B) → ~(A → ~B)  and  (A → ~B) → ~(A → B),

are valid, and in which → is in general not contraposable. Define the contraposable conditional ⇒ in C by

  A ⇒ B  :=  (A → B) ∧ (~B → ~A).

Recall that Spinks and Veroff showed that constructive logic with strong negation (Nelson's logic N3) is term-equivalent to a certain substructural / relevant logic, by isolating a contraction-free relevant conditional definable inside N3, and used this to systematically study extensions of N3 that correspond to relevance logics.

Problem. Carry out an analogous systematic investigation for C and its natural extensions/variants (for example C with weakening, contraction, or other structural axioms; extensions by additional connexive principles; and finite-valued or matrix-based variants of C), where the role of the primitive conditional is replaced by the contraposable conditional ⇒. Specifically:

(a) Identify which axiomatic extensions and structural variants of C, when reformulated with ⇒ as their basic conditional, yield logics that are translationally equivalent (or otherwise tightly related, e.g. via definitional or term equivalence) to known relevance logics or to substructural logics in the vicinity of R, RW, T, or contraction-free relevant logics.

(b) For each such system, determine the precise correspondence (axiomatization, algebraic semantics, and consequence relation) between the C-style presentation and the relevance-logic-style presentation.

(c) Single out those C-related systems that are "especially interesting" in the sense that the focus on the contraposable conditional ⇒ reveals a substantive connection to relevance logics, and classify them.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as one of ten open problems in connexive logic and asks for an open-ended systematic program. Recent work (e.g., on relevant acceptable strictly connexive logics, 2026) continues to investigate connections between connexive logic C and relevance logics, but no comprehensive Spinks–Veroff-style classification of C-related systems via the contraposable conditional appears to have been carried out. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Ten Open Problems in Connexive Logic
status_evidence.snippet: Lists ten open problems including the systematic investigation of C-related systems via the contraposable conditional and their connections to relevance logics.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On Relevant Acceptable Strictly Connexive Logics
status_evidence.snippet: Recent investigation of connections between connexive logics and relevance logics.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research connects connexive and relevance logics, but does not present a Spinks–Veroff-style systematic classification for C.

status_evidence.title: Connexive Logic (SEP)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses C, contraposable conditional, and relations to relevance logic without reporting a complete systematic Spinks–Veroff-style program for C.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys do not report the program as completed.
